articles.title: Husband’s ‘Heart Attack’ Was Murder: Wife, Lover Killed Him for ₹2 Crore Insurance
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Shocking details have emerged in the Pallati Ramesh murder case that rocked Nizamabad district. What was initially believed to be a heart attack has now been confirmed as a planned murder, police said.

body.html:
Shocking details have emerged in the Pallati Ramesh murder case that rocked Nizamabad district. What was initially believed to be a heart attack has now been confirmed as a planned murder, police said.

Investigations revealed that Ramesh’s wife, Soumya, along with her boyfriend Dilip, allegedly murdered him to continue their extramarital relationship and claim an insurance amount of nearly ₹2 crore. Police said Soumya planned the murder to eliminate her husband and gain financially.

According to officials, Ramesh was first given sleeping pills to make him unconscious. He was then strangled to death by the accused, who attempted to pass the killing off as a natural death. Funeral preparations were also made, believing the crime had gone unnoticed.

However, suspicion raised by Ramesh’s younger brother led to a police complaint. A re-postmortem confirmed death due to strangulation, not a heart attack. During interrogation, both Soumya and Dilip confessed to the crime.

Police have arrested both accused and sent them to judicial remand. The case has sparked widespread discussion in the region, highlighting how greed and an extramarital affair led to a brutal murder.

articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A disturbing video of an Indian family has gone viral on social media, showing a father being verbally abused and allegedly assaulted by his daughter in front of his wife. The video has triggered widespread outrage online.

body.html:
A disturbing video of an Indian family has gone viral on social media, showing a father being verbally abused and allegedly assaulted by his daughter in front of his wife. The video has triggered widespread outrage online.

According to claims circulating on X, the mother and daughter allegedly spent the father’s hard-earned savings on gambling and stock market investments. After suffering heavy losses, they reportedly blamed the father for mismanaging finances.

In the video, the daughter is seen hurling abuses at her father, accusing him of failing as a parent and provider. She is also seen pushing him and attempting to hit him, while the mother remains present and appears supportive or silent. The woman filming the incident tries to intervene but is also spoken to rudely.

The exact location of the incident remains unverified. The clip was widely shared in early January 2026 by multiple X accounts, including @NCMIndiaa and @CartelFights, with captions criticising the treatment of the father.

The video has sparked intense debate online, with users condemning gambling and reckless financial behaviour, while others called for the matter to be resolved privately within the family. Many viewers described the clip as a grim reminder of how gambling and speculative investments can destroy families.

Note: The faces of all family members in the video have been blurred to protect their dignity and privacy.

articles.title: Viral Mystery Solved: Why a ‘Shocked Woman’ Poster Keeps Appearing at Bengaluru Construction Sites
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: An ordinary commute turned into an internet mystery for a Maharashtrian woman living in Bengaluru, after she repeatedly noticed the same striking poster hanging from construction sites across the city and nearby parts of Karnataka.

body.html:
An ordinary commute turned into an internet mystery for a Maharashtrian woman living in Bengaluru, after she repeatedly noticed the same striking poster hanging from construction sites across the city and nearby parts of Karnataka.

X user @unitechy, who frequently travels across the state, observed a recurring image of a saree-clad woman with wide, kohl-lined eyes and a visibly shocked expression displayed on half-built buildings. The poster appeared so consistently that it piqued her curiosity. After failing to identify the woman using Google Lens, she decided to seek answers online.

On January 5, 2026, she posted about the mystery on X (formerly Twitter), asking why the same woman’s image was being used at construction sites across Karnataka. The post quickly went viral, amassing over 3.5 million views and triggering widespread debate and speculation.

Several users offered cultural explanations, suggesting the image functions as a “nazar battu” or “dristi gombe”—a traditional symbol used to ward off the evil eye and protect properties from negative energy. Such charms are commonly seen at construction sites, though they typically feature exaggerated or grotesque faces rather than realistic human expressions. Some users speculated that the image represents a modern, meme-inspired evolution of this age-old practice.

The mystery took a new turn when an X user shared a screenshot from an AI chatbot, which identified the woman as Niharika Rao, a Karnataka-based YouTuber. According to the chatbot, the image originated from a 2023 viral video clip in which her shocked reaction became a popular meme. Over time, locals allegedly adopted the image humorously as a protective charm, blending superstition with internet culture.

While many commenters leaned into spiritual and cultural interpretations, others treated the phenomenon light-heartedly. One user joked that the image was a “demonic sigil” meant to scare off thieves. As more people began spotting the poster across Bengaluru markets and nearby towns, the image only gained further attention online.

What began as a routine observation during daily travel has now become a viral example of how traditional beliefs and digital meme culture are increasingly intersecting in urban India.

What do you think—superstition, meme culture, or both? Comment below.

articles.title: Delhi vs Mumbai Debate Reignited After Viral Reddit Post Calls Delhi More Livable
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A detailed Reddit post by a professional who recently lived in Mumbai after spending most of his life in Delhi NCR has gone viral, once again fuelling the long-running Delhi vs Mumbai debate.

body.html:
A detailed Reddit post by a professional who recently lived in Mumbai after spending most of his life in Delhi NCR has gone viral, once again fuelling the long-running Delhi vs Mumbai debate. Shared on Reddit’s Delhi Community, the post compares the two cities on cost of living, infrastructure, healthcare, commuting, and the often-cited “spirit of Mumbai.”

The author described Mumbai’s cost of living as his biggest shock, calling the city “insanely expensive.” He claimed he was quoted ₹25,000 for a single-sharing room “barely big enough to stand in,” while friends in Delhi NCR pay ₹12,000–₹15,000 for an entire 1RK or 1BHK. According to him, even suburban Mumbai rents for a 1BHK easily cross ₹40,000, whereas the same budget in Delhi can fetch a spacious 3BHK or even an independent house.

Despite staying in a premium locality like Juhu, he said daily commuting involved traffic congestion, bad smells, and constant chaos. He added that traffic becomes unbearable during monsoons, with flooding affecting not just slums but also middle-class and upscale areas.

The post also criticised Mumbai’s healthcare system, alleging that consultation fees are significantly higher than in Delhi, while doctors in the national capital appear academically stronger on average.

A major point of contention was what the author called “denial” among long-time Mumbaikars. He wrote that overcrowded local trains are romanticised as “love” and “spirit,” crushing rents are worn as a badge of pride, and slums are framed as symbols of resilience rather than systemic failure.

The post triggered intense reactions online. Several users agreed with the criticism, with one saying people who deny Mumbai’s flaws prefer to stay in denial. Another user claimed there is “absolutely no comparison” with Delhi’s infrastructure, food, and public transport.

Interestingly, some Mumbaikars also echoed similar sentiments. One user wrote that after spending a year in Delhi, they now agree with many of the criticisms of Mumbai. Another lifelong resident admitted loving the city for personal memories but feeling exhausted by current conditions.

The debate also spilled into stereotypes about people from both cities. While one user called Delhiites “fake,” others strongly defended Delhi, saying its people are straightforward and honest, even if sometimes rude.

As the post continues to gain traction, it has once again highlighted the stark contrasts—and emotional loyalties—attached to India’s two biggest metros.

What’s your take on the Delhi vs Mumbai debate? Comment below. (Link: https://www.reddit.com/r/delhi/comments/1q4jyja/)

articles.title: Dark Secrets of a ‘Godman’: Dera Head Sevadar Baba Baljinder Singh Gets 10 Years Jail for
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Baba Baljinder Singh, the head sevadar of Gurdwara Thath Charan Ghat in Jagraon, Ludhiana, has been sentenced to 10 years’ rigorous imprisonment by the Moga District Court in a r@pe case.

body.html:
Baba Baljinder Singh, the head sevadar of Gurdwara Thath Charan Ghat in Jagraon, Ludhiana, has been sentenced to 10 years’ rigorous imprisonment by the Moga District Court in a r@pe case.

According to police and court records, a woman accused Baljinder Singh of sexually exploiting her over a long period on the pretext of marriage. She alleged that he called her to hotels and rooms inside the dera, established physical relations, and later threatened her when she demanded marriage. The victim also claimed she received repeated threats and was offered ₹10 lakh to silence the matter.

The woman stated she had initially approached the sevadar regarding a family problem and remained in contact with him for nearly two years. She further alleged that Baljinder Singh assaulted her after she questioned his conduct with other women.

Investigations revealed that Baljinder Singh lived alone in a private room at the dera, where he met followers individually under strict control. He was known to claim he could cure serious diseases and resolve personal problems through prayers, allegations that later came under scrutiny.

Baljinder Singh has faced multiple controversies in the past. In 2021, an FIR was registered against him over alleged sacrilege during a Nagar Kirtan. In 2024, he was accused of r@pe by a woman in Jagraon but was acquitted in that case. However, in the Moga case, the court found him guilty and awarded a 10-year jail term.

Police said incriminating materials were earlier recovered from his room during searches. The accused has been sent to jail following the verdict.

articles.title: ‘Fake Treasure’ Exposed in Rajasthan: Gold-Plated Brass Bricks Found in 150-kg Pot, Two Arrested
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: What was believed to be a cache of ancient treasure in Rajasthan’s Tonk district has turned out to be an elaborate fraud. Police have arrested two men after a silver pot unearthed near Niwai was found to contain fake gold bricks and counterfeit jewellery.

body.html:
What was believed to be a cache of ancient treasure in Rajasthan’s Tonk district has turned out to be an elaborate fraud. Police have arrested two men after a silver pot unearthed near Niwai was found to contain fake gold bricks and counterfeit jewellery.

The pot, weighing around 150 kg, was discovered during land excavation in a village pasture, triggering rumours of hidden wealth and drawing large crowds. However, police investigation revealed that the vessel contained brass bricks coated with gold plating weighing over 5 kg, fake biscuits and old artificial jewellery that had been deliberately buried.

The accused, Mukesh Meena (32) and Abhishek Meena (24) of Seedra village, allegedly planted the items to exploit villagers’ greed. Mukesh posed as “Tatkal Aghori Maharaj” on social media and lured people with claims of dhan siddhi (hidden treasure), performing fake rituals and demanding money while advising victims not to open the pot for days.

Niwai DSP Ravi Prakash Sharma confirmed the arrests and said the recovered items were not gold. Tonk SP Rajesh Kumar Meena has constituted a team to probe possible occult links and the wider network. The pot has been sealed and kept in the sub-treasury for further examination.

articles.title: Inter-Caste Love Marriage Sparks Street Attack in Chikkaballapur, Shocking Twist at Police Station
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Tension prevailed near Mayura Circle in Sidlaghatta town of Chikkaballapur district after a newly married inter-caste couple was allegedly attacked by the woman’s family members.

body.html:
Tension prevailed near Mayura Circle in Sidlaghatta town of Chikkaballapur district after a newly married inter-caste couple was allegedly attacked by the woman’s family members.

The couple, Sandeep (24) from the ST community and Keerthana (19) from the Balijiga community, had been in a relationship for about a year. After leaving their homes two days ago, they reportedly got married at the Kotagal Narasimhaswamy temple in Chintamani taluk.

Police said the woman’s parents had earlier filed a missing complaint. On Tuesday, when the couple was travelling towards the police station, the woman’s family allegedly intercepted their car near Sidlaghatta, smashed its glass and tried to forcibly take her away. The woman reportedly refused to go with her parents, insisting she would stay with her husband.

However, during questioning at the police station, police records reportedly revealed that Sandeep was named in previous cases, including a 2024 case involving an underage girl, a cheating case, and a POCSO case registered in Bengaluru. Another alleged victim also arrived at the police station and gave a statement.

Following these developments, the newly married woman reportedly removed her mangalsutra and left with her family members. A case has been registered at the Chikkaballapur Women’s Police Station, and police said further investigation is underway.

articles.title: Caretaker Found Murdered in Sonipat Marriage Palace, Wife Accused After Marital Dispute
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A 38-year-old man was allegedly murdered by his wife inside a marriage palace in Sonipat, Haryana, police said on Tuesday. The deceased, Ramkishan, worked as a caretaker at Ashirwad Garden, where he lived with his family.

body.html:
A 38-year-old man was allegedly murdered by his wife inside a marriage palace in Sonipat, Haryana, police said on Tuesday. The deceased, Ramkishan, worked as a caretaker at Ashirwad Garden, where he lived with his family.

According to the family, Ramkishan’s wife Sarita allegedly smothered him with a pillow and fled the spot. His body was found lying on the bed on Tuesday morning. The couple reportedly had frequent quarrels, allegedly over Sarita’s illicit relationship.

On receiving information around 9 am, ACP Amit reached the spot with a police team, and a forensic unit was called for investigation. CCTV footage from the marriage palace has been seized, and the body has been sent to the civil hospital for post-mortem.

Ramkishan had been living in Sonipat for the past two years and is survived by three minor sons. His brother Mehar Singh alleged that Sarita, along with another man named Satpal, was involved in the murder. Police said both have been named as accused in the FIR.

ACP Amit said the case is being investigated from all angles, and further action will be taken after the post-mortem report.

articles.title: Burglary Goes Wrong: Thief Gets Stuck in Exhaust Fan Hole for Hours in Kota
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: In a bizarre incident in Rajasthan’s Kota city, a burglar attempting to break into a locked house got trapped in an exhaust fan opening and remained stuck there for several hours. The incident took place in Pratap Nagar when a family had gone out of town to visit Khatu Shyam Ji.

body.html:
In a bizarre incident in Rajasthan’s Kota city, a burglar attempting to break into a locked house got trapped in an exhaust fan opening and remained stuck there for several hours.

The incident took place in Pratap Nagar when a family had gone out of town to visit Khatu Shyam Ji. Taking advantage of the locked house, two thieves allegedly attempted a burglary late at night. While one managed to escape, the other, identified as Subhash, tried to enter the house through an exhaust fan opening but got badly stuck, with half his body inside and half outside.

The family returned home the next day and found the thief trapped in the window, struggling to free himself. They immediately raised an alarm and informed the police. Locals gathered at the spot before police arrived and rescued the accused after considerable effort.

Police said no theft had taken place as the accused got stuck while preparing for the burglary. The thief was later arrested and questioned. A video of the incident has gone viral on social media. Police also revealed that the accused had come with the intention of stealing a vehicle fitted with a police sticker.
